process: D20: two blind graders (D7), adjudicator on disagreements, agent audit of agreed verdicts (D11)

verdicts.reason: The view is not only a value judgment: telework expansion and work spilling into non-work time are measured. Both moved in the stated direction but modestly: ATUS share doing some work at home on workdays rose 19% (2003) to 23% (2014), and Pew 2014 found 35% of online workers say technology increased their hours. A real but minority blurring, not a significant erosion; 'sharply alter family dynamics' has no measure and is not graded. Held in part. Grader A's ungradable discards the measurable half.

The statement has no geographic limit, so the global reading dominates. RAND (2014) counted Salafi-jihadist groups rising 58% (31 to 49) 2010-2013 with fighters more than doubling, and ISIS drew tens of thousands of foreign fighters largely via online propaganda by 2014-15. Grader B's SPLC count of US hate groups (784 in 2014) is a US formal-group measure; SPLC itself attributes the drop to migration online, which fits the 'networks flourish online' clause rather than refuting growth.

The forecast's payoff, and the reason the statement exists, is higher social trust; network growth is the stated mechanism. Trust fell: GSS 'most people can be trusted' about 34% in 2018-2024, below mid-2000s GSS levels, and 71% of Americans in 2019 said interpersonal trust had declined. The consequence failed, so the view misses. Grader B's baseline is a reading error: the 44-45% figure for 2006 is from Pew's own 2006 survey, not the GSS, so the 44%-to-34% drop compares two different surveys (direction still holds on GSS alone).

The statement's headline is further polarization; filtering is its mechanism. The majority's rejection held on filtering: only about 21% of Americans were consistent ideologues with insulated media diets in 2014. It failed on polarization: partisan antipathy more than doubled 1994-2014 and the most polarized were also the most filtered. Grader A's hit grades only the 'most people filter' clause and drops the polarization clause the respondents also rejected.

The defining content of the rejected scenario is dangers 'not recognized until it is impossible to reverse them', which has no public measure. Grader B graded a narrower proxy (autonomous weapons) that the text does not name; for the named activities, fully automated pipelines did exist by 2020 (algorithmic mass surveillance, automated trading and content filtering), so even the proxy does not clearly support a hit. Looked for incident databases; they record recognized harms only.

Text says 'the only one for a majority of the people across the world'. Primary held: 92% of 4.54B internet users connected via mobile and mobile broadband (75 per 100) far exceeded fixed (about 15 per 100). 'Only one for a majority of the world' did not: only about 51-58% of the world was online at all, and three-quarters of users 16-64 also used computers, so mobile-only users were well under half the world's population. Grader A's reading drops the 'only one' clause.

The boundary claim is measurable even though 'net positive' is not (not graded). In 2020, 71% of telework-capable US workers worked from home all or most of the time and 49% of new teleworkers had more freedom over hours, so boundaries blurred widely; but it was pandemic-forced, not willing, only 38% found work-life balance easier, and right-to-disconnect laws (France 2017 onward) show boundaries were being restored, not erased. Held in part. Same treatment as 2005-004.

A causal judgment about the internet's net effect on three things; no public measure isolates it. Indicators point both ways: NAEP reading scores declined from 2015 (against), while the volume of writing and open reference works such as Wikipedia grew (for 'rendering of knowledge'). Grader B graded only test-score literacy and dropped 'rendering of knowledge'; NAEP cannot attribute the decline to internet use. Looked for NAEP and literacy trend data.

Both graders agree no verdict is possible; the question is which non-verdict. D16 unfalsifiable requires readings that each give a verdict. Here neither the product reading nor the category reading can be scored, because no public record exists of what 2010's 'savviest innovators' anticipated, and 'often' has no count. That is D22 ungradable. Looked for: a record of 2010 innovator expectations against 2020 hit products.

Not only a value judgment: the scenario makes a specific factual claim ('they do not suffer notable cognitive shortcomings as they multitask'), and the research record by 2018 went against it: heavy media multitaskers perform worse in several cognitive domains (Ophir 2009; Uncapher and Wagner 2018 review), consistent with option B's 'distracted, do not retain'. The review calls causation inconclusive, but the claim concerns shortcomings, not their cause. 'Wired differently' and 'positive overall' are not graded. Low confidence.

An adoption claim under D16 plus a displacement state. Mobile payment reached a measurable share: 46% of US consumers made at least one mobile payment in the 12 months to Oct 2020 (38% in 2019). The displacement failed: cash, debit and credit still made about three-quarters of US payments (19%, 28%, 27%). Adoption grew well past 5% while the stated end-state did not arrive, which is a partial, not a miss. Grader A's 'roughly a quarter' adoption figure was unsourced; the Fed figure is 46% for any mobile payment.

Both graders agree the measurable clause held: central banks routinely publish big-data nowcasts (Atlanta Fed GDPNow from 2014, NY Fed nowcast) with alternative-data and ML inputs. Under D22/D27 an unmeasurable clause is not graded; it cannot count against the view. Grader A downgraded to partial for the ungraded value clause, which mixes the two rules. Note: the factual clause is shared by option B, so the hit says little about the panel's real split.

BLS chart confirms US unemployment 4.0-4.4% Jan-Sep 2025, but aggregate unemployment does not measure jobs displaced vs created by AI and robots; no public series measures that balance, so the evidence is a proxy of another quantity (D22/D23) and supports neither hit nor miss.

Read 'at the levels of tens of billions' as an order of magnitude, the dominant reading of a definitional threshold. NotPetya (2017), a Russian military operation, disabled Ukrainian ministries, banks, metro, energy and telecoms and caused over $10B in damage per the White House. That meets both the national-security and the scale test, at the lower edge. Grader B's partial rests on reading 'tens' as at least $20B; defensible but the narrower reading.

The option is an explicit comparison with early 2020, not a counterfactual (the counterfactual is the third option), so it is measurable on population-level wellbeing. Global HDI hit a record high in 2023 and kept rising; Gallup's 2024 global thriving median (33%) is higher than before the pandemic and suffering (7%) matches the record low. Life was not mostly worse for most people. Uneven recovery in about half of LDCs affects a minority of people.
